verses.english: The world saw you plunging into the armies [and] fighting with the Pāṇḍavas, great chariot-warriors of surpassing splendour.
verses.gold_issues: form अनुदृष्टवन् should be अनुदृष्टवान्; अति tagged as free ADP, it is the first member of the bahuvrīhi अतितेजस्.

verses.text: तत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वा मासि मासि जनेश्वर । अभिगच्छन्ति तत्तीर्थं पुण्यं ब्राह्मणसेवितम् ॥
verses.english: O lord of men, there, month after month, the gods together with the Gandharvas visit that holy tīrtha frequented by Brahmins.
verses.gold_issues: स (सह) tagged as free ADV, not compound member.

verses.text: अरण्ये यो विमुञ्चेत संग्रामे वा तनुं नरः । क्रतूनाहृत्य महतो महिमानं स गच्छति ॥
verses.english: The man who would give up his body in the forest or in battle — he, [as if] having performed great sacrifices, attains greatness.
verses.gold_issues: विमुञ्चेत tagged Person=2 Number=Plur; it is 3rd sg. optative (ātmanepada).

verses.text: नातः पुण्यतरं दानं नातः पुण्यतरं फलम् । नातो विशिष्टं लोकेषु भूतं भवितुमर्हति ॥
verses.english: There is no gift holier than this, no fruit holier than this; no being in the worlds can be superior to this.
verses.gold_issues: अतः used in ablative sense (standard of comparison) but tagged ADV; annotated अव्यय.

compounds.vigraha: हुताशनस्य ज्वलिताः शिखाः इव उज्ज्वलन्ती प्रभा यस्य तत्
शरदि अमलस्य अर्कस्य तेजः इव तेजः यस्य तत्

verses.english: The lotus of the great-souled one shines, [now] present, its radiance blazing like the flaming crests of fire, with the brilliance of the spotless autumn sun, of noble lustre, lovely to behold with its filaments.
verses.gold_issues: प्रभम्, उपस्थितम्, तेजसम् tagged Acc but agree with nominative कमलम् (Nom); तेजसम् Gender=Masc should be Neut.

verses.text: को हि मे भोक्तुकामस्य विघ्नं चरति दुर्मतिः । न बिभेषि हिडिम्बे किं मत्कोपाद्विप्रमोहिता ॥
verses.english: Who indeed, evil-minded, makes an obstacle for me who wish to eat? Hiḍimbā, deluded, do you not fear my anger?
verses.gold_issues: भोक्तु given as NOUN lemma; it is the infinitive भोक्तुम् with -म् dropped before काम. मत्कोपात् = feared thing with भी (अपादान).

verses.text: विहगाश्च मुदा युक्ताः प्रानृत्यन्व्यनदंश्च ह । गिरिपृष्ठेषु रम्येषु व्याहरन्तो जनप्रियाः ॥
verses.english: And the birds, filled with joy, dear to people, calling out on the lovely mountain-ridges, danced and indeed cried out.

verses.text: एकादशचमूभर्ता सो ऽहमेतां दशां गतः । कालं प्राप्य महाबाहो न कश्चिदतिवर्तते ॥
verses.english: I, that lord of eleven armies, have come to this state; O mighty-armed one, no one, having met [his] time, escapes [it].

verses.text: चिन्तयञ्जलमध्यस्थो मार्कण्डेयो विशङ्कितः । किं नु स्यान्मम चिन्तेयं मोहः स्वप्नोऽनुभूयते ॥
verses.english: Thinking, Mārkaṇḍeya, standing in the midst of the waters, became apprehensive: "What could this thought of mine be? Is a delusion, a dream, being experienced?"
verses.gold_issues: the quoted question is the content of चिन्तयन् (no इति); heads attached to चिन्तयन्.

verses.text: तावच्चात्र प्रतिष्ठाने प्राविशत्तस्य सा प्रिया । चिरप्रविष्टं तं कान्तं वीक्षितुं देवसद्म तत् ॥
verses.english: And meanwhile, here in Pratiṣṭhāna, his beloved entered that temple to see her lover, who had entered long before.

verses.text: महानात्मा मतिर्विष्णुर्विश्वः शंभुश्च वीर्यवान् । बुद्धिः प्रज्ञोपलब्धिश्च तथा ख्यातिर्धृतिः स्मृतिः ॥
verses.english: [It is called] Mahat, Ātman, Mati, Viṣṇu, Viśva and mighty Śambhu, Buddhi, Prajñā and Upalabdhi, likewise Khyāti, Dhṛti, Smṛti.
verses.gold_issues: form/lemma महन्त् is odd (महान्, lemma महत्). महान् might alternatively qualify आत्मा (विशेषण>1); taken as a separate name in this list of synonyms.

verses.text: नित्योदको ब्राह्मणः स्यान्नित्यशस्त्रश्च क्षत्रियः । तयोर्हि सर्वमायत्तं यत्किंचिज्जगतीगतम् ॥
verses.english: A Brahmin should be one who always has water [at hand], and a Kṣatriya one who always bears a weapon; for everything whatsoever that exists on earth depends on these two.

verses.text: अर्चयित्वा जामदग्न्यं पूजितस्तेन चाभिभूः । महेन्द्र उष्य तां रात्रिं प्रययौ दक्षिणामुखः ॥
verses.english: Having worshipped Jāmadagnya [and] been honoured by him, [the lord], having spent that night on Mahendra, set out facing south.
verses.gold_issues: the text's च and अभिभूः (चाभिभूः) are missing from the word list. रात्रिम् is accusative of duration (annotated कर्म of उष्य).

verses.text: याचकेभ्यो ददौ नित्यं वित्तं यावच्च यच्च सः । दृष्टा मदनमाला सा तत्तस्मै स्वमुपानयत् ॥
verses.english: He always gave wealth to beggars, as much and whatever [he had]; Madanamālā, seen [by him], brought that [wealth] of her own to him.
verses.gold_issues: यावत् tagged SCONJ; here an adverb of quantity paired with यत्.

verses.text: शराणां धनुषश्चाहमनृणो ऽस्मि महावने । ससैन्यं भरतं हत्वा भविष्यामि न संशयः ॥
verses.english: In the great forest I am free of debt to [my] arrows and bow; having slain Bharata together with his army I shall be [so]; there is no doubt.
verses.gold_issues: स tagged as free ADV, not compound member. Two finite verbs (अस्मि, भविष्यामि) with अनृणः shared.
